symptom: On macOS, the app in the DMG fails codesign --verify --strict because of Finder info detritus.
toml:
known_fixed = ["pdfcraft", "vectorcraft"]
references = ["storytold/pdfcraft#823", "storytold/vectorcraft#1121"]
title = "Build the macOS DMG with hdiutil create -srcfolder instead of makehybrid"
why = 'Building the DMG with `hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` gives every file a com.apple.FinderInfo attribute. Because of that, the app inside the image and any copy installed from it fail `codesign --verify --strict` with a "Finder information, or similar detritus" error, and MDM and compliance checks report a correctly notarized app as damaged.'

[[applies_if]]
grep = "^[^#]*hdiutil "
in = ["packaging/**", "**/*.sh"]

[exempt]

[[fixed_if]]
grep = "^[^#]*hdiutil[^#]*-srcfolder"
in = ["packaging/**", "**/*.sh", ".github/**"]

[[proof]]
app = "pdfcraft"
pr = 823

[[proof]]
app = "vectorcraft"
pr = 1121
reasoning:
Before the fix, each app built its DMG with `hdiutil makehybrid` plus `convert`. The fix replaces that with `hdiutil create -srcfolder`, run through a retry wrapper, and then checks the app on the mounted image with `codesign --verify --strict --deep`.

**What the fixes share.** Every fix makes an hdiutil call that uses `-srcfolder`, so that is the marker.

**Why comment lines are excluded.** Before the fix, pdfcraft already had a comment mentioning `create -srcfolder`. The regex skips lines that start with `#` before the match, so that comment can't make an unfixed app pass.

**Checks I left out:**
- **`--deep` verify:** `codesign --verify --strict --deep` may already appear elsewhere for the plain app bundle, so it wouldn't reliably fail before the fix.
- **Mount-and-check step:** an app that ports the fix may do this step differently, for example in a CI workflow instead of the packaging script.

**When the fingerprint applies:** to any app whose packaging scripts call hdiutil, meaning it builds a macOS DMG.

cadcraft.evidence:
packaging/macos/package.sh:
hdiutil makehybrid -hfs -hfs-volume-name "CADCraft" -hfs-openfolder "$STAGE" -o "$WORK/raw.dmg" "$STAGE"
hdiutil convert "$WORK/raw.dmg" -format UDZO -imagekey zlib-level=9 -o "$DMG"
sign "$DMG"
codesign --verify --strict --verbose=2 "$DMG"
cadcraft.explanation: CADCraft still builds its DMG with `hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` followed by `convert`. That is the same unfixed code the sibling had. As a result, every file in the image gets a com.apple.FinderInfo attribute, and the app inside fails `codesign --verify --strict`. The script never mounts the DMG to check the app inside with --strict. It only verifies the DMG's own signature, so the problem isn't caught.

craft-launcher.evidence:
packaging/macos/package.sh:
hdiutil makehybrid -hfs -hfs-volume-name "$APP_NAME $VERSION" -hfs-openfolder "$STAGE" -o "$WORK/raw.dmg" "$STAGE"
hdiutil convert "$WORK/raw.dmg" -format UDZO -imagekey zlib-level=9 -o "$DMG"

packaging/macos/verify.sh:
# Integrity first: ... Not --strict here: files read back from
# the DMG's HFS volume (hdiutil makehybrid) report a com.apple.FinderInfo attribute, which strict
# mode calls "detritus".
codesign --verify --deep --verbose=2 "$APP"
craft-launcher.explanation: craft-launcher still builds its DMG with `hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` and then `convert`, just like the sibling did before its fix. It does not use `hdiutil create -srcfolder`. This puts the com.apple.FinderInfo attribute on the app inside the image, so `codesign --verify --strict` fails on it and on any copy installed from it. verify.sh even says so in a comment: it leaves out `--strict` on the mounted app because of this "detritus". That hides the problem rather than fixing it. Users' MDM and compliance checks would still report the app as damaged.
